implPrompt: Read .claude/ralph.md and follow the rules in that file. Implement GitHub issue #{issue} ("{title}") from milestone '{milestone}'. You are already on branch {branch}: work there, do not create or switch branches. When the work is done and all tests pass, commit it and close issue #{issue}. Do not open a pull request and do not start another issue.
reviewPrompt:
Review the work of milestone '{milestone}'. The diff to review is the output of `git diff {range}` - the phase branch {branch} against the feature branch {featureBranch}. Read the PRD and phase plan under docs/ for the feature, then check the diff for correctness, architecture, security, performance and test coverage.

Sort every finding into one of two buckets.

BLOCKING - the phase must not ship with it: a bug, a security or data-integrity problem, a missing acceptance criterion, or a design decision that later phases would have to work around. File one GitHub issue per blocking finding in milestone '{milestone}', so the loop implements the fix, and end your reply with a line containing only BLOCKED.

NON-BLOCKING - worth doing but not now: naming, small refactors, extra test cases, documentation polish. File one GitHub issue per finding with the label '{niceToHaveLabel}' and NO milestone, so it stays in the backlog for a separate pass and does not hold up this phase.

When nothing is blocking, end your reply with a line containing only APPROVED - even if you filed nice-to-have issues. Be strict about the split: treating polish as blocking sends the loop into endless rework. Do not commit, push, merge or open a pull request.
